 ​Cyclonic Circulation Forms Over South Andaman Sea; IMD Forecasts Minimal Impact and Dry Weather for Odisha Till November 21
 by 
 Ananya Pattnaik 
 November 12, 2026 
 in 
 Odisha , Trending Now 
 Reading Time: 1 min read
 0 
 0 
 0 
 291 
 VIEWS 
 A fresh cyclonic circulation formed over the South Andaman Sea on Wednesday, November 11, 2026, and is projected to intensify into a depression over the Bay of Bengal by November 15, according to the India Meteorological Department (IMD).
 ​Despite the developing weather system, the IMD has confirmed that Odisha is unlikely to experience any significant adverse weather, bringing major relief to the state’s residents and coastal districts.
 ​ System Trajectory & Intensification Timeline 
 ​According to the IMD’s regional meteorological bulletin, the weather system will follow a north-westerly trajectory over the next several days:
 ​ November 13 (Low-Pressure Area): Moving northwestward, the cyclonic circulation is likely to concentrate into a low-pressure area over the southeast Bay of Bengal.
 ​ November 14 (Well-Marked Low): The system is expected to gain further strength and organize into a well-marked low-pressure area.
 ​ November 15 (Depression): Continued favorable atmospheric conditions over the sea are projected to intensify the system into a depression by Sunday, November 15.
 Odisha Weather Outlook Through November 21 
 ​Meteorological models indicate that the system’s path will steer clear of the Odisha coast, keeping atmospheric conditions stable across the state:
 ​ Mainly Dry Conditions (Till Nov 17): Dry weather is forecast to prevail across all interior and coastal districts of Odisha through November 17, with no rainfall or cyclonic warnings issued for the state.
 ​ Extended Stability (Nov 18 – Nov 21): No major shifts in weather patterns or significant rainfall activity are anticipated across Odisha between November 18 and November 21.
